## Dimorphos’s Orbit Continued to Change After DART

Dimorphos, the smaller asteroid orbiting Didymos, completed an orbit in 11 hours and 55 minutes before DART’s impact. Its orbital period was shorter immediately after the impact, then shortened further over the following weeks. During that time, Dimorphos also lost more rocky material to space; the observations do not establish that this loss caused the continued shortening.

The period eventually settled at about 11 hours and 22 minutes—roughly 33 minutes shorter than before the impact. Dimorphos’s orbit was also no longer circular.
